name: SLICE (Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment)
objective: Understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity, including liftoff velocity limits for different fuels and burner diameters.
hardware: Fan-driven flow duct with exchangeable burner tubes (Microgravity Science Glovebox)
sensors: Flow rate and temperature sensors; high-resolution camera
variables: Burner diameter, coflow velocity, fuel composition

name: ACME Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G)
objective: Determine the conditions under which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane and n-pentane.
hardware: ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (ISS)
variables: Reactant dilution, flow rate, pressure, flow direction

name: ACME Flame Design
objective: Obtain soot-inception limits of spherical diffusion flames as functions of flow rate and dilution.
hardware: ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (ISS); drop towers
variables: Reactant dilution, flow rate, pressure, flow direction

name: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
objective: Understand why soot formation differs between normal-gravity and microgravity flames.
sensors: Camera images analysed with color-ratio pyrometry

name: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling with Comparison to BASS Experiments
objective: Develop and validate flamelet-based models of concurrent flame spread in microgravity.
sensors: Two-color tomography of BASS and BASS-II imagery

name: External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics
objective: Use FLEX flight data to quantify how external thermal and convective perturbations affect cool flame dynamics.
